thread.title: Chip Stocks Struggle Under Weight Of Negative News

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Chip Stocks Struggle Under Weight Of Negative News

organizations.name: chip stocks struggle under weight of negative news chip

text:
Chip stocks tanked Thursday as investors weighed a lowered outlook for the sector from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM ) and other negative data points. At least one Wall Street analyst thinks investors overreacted.
X In a report Friday, Needham analyst Rajvindra Gill said the broad sell-off was not justified.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped 4.3% on Thursday. It was the biggest one-day drop for the index, known as SOX, since Feb. 8 and only the tenth time in the past eight years where the index fell more than 4%.
The iShares PHLX Semiconductor ETF ( SOXX ) fell 1.2% on the stock market today .

Please contact customer service CLOSE Several concerns led to the broad sell-off on Thursday, Gill said. They included Taiwan Semi's weak near-term guidance and reduced annual forecast for the semiconductor industry, plus renewed concerns about customers double ordering, he said.
Investors also reacted to China's hesitance to approve Qualcomm 's ( QCOM ) takeover of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ), citing competition concerns.
Investors are worried that chip stocks have passed the top of the current up cycle and could be headed down, Gill said.
Taiwan Semi blamed its lowered guidance on smartphone demand weakness, particularly at Apple ( AAPL ), and cryptocurrency mining volatility. Conversely the company noted strength in chips for automotive, Internet of Things and high-performance computing, Gill said.
Investors would be wise to avoid chip companies in Apple's iPhone supply chain, but should stick with chip firms with exposure to automotive, industrial and data-center markets, Gill said.
Apple chip suppliers include Cirrus Logic ( CRUS ) and Tower Semiconductor ( TSEM ), he said.
In the auto, industrial and data center markets, Gill likes Cypress Semiconductor ( CY ), Microchip Technology ( MCHP ), Nvidia ( NVDA ), ON Semiconductor ( ON ) and Silicon Laboratories ( SLAB ).
